clue.text: Return message by heliograph — a cinematic device

definitions.meaning: a heliograph signals with flashes of sunlight
a film cut to an earlier scene in the story

explanation.surface: A signaller's sunlit reply is compared to a film technique.
explanation.definitionFit: A film scene that jumps back in time is this device, and a heliograph operator replying would literally flash a message back.

clue.text: In which the subject will be clearly defined

definitions.text: In which the subject will be clearly defined

parts.words: In which the subject will be clearly defined
parts.note: a photographer's sharp setting, in which the person photographed appears crisp, not a teacher's lesson

explanation.surface: A teacher's lesson plan making the topic clear.
explanation.definitionFit: A camera or lens set sharp renders the image clearly.

clue.text: Platonic type of defence that admits guilt?

definitions.text: Platonic type of defence that admits guilt?

parts.words: Platonic type of defence that admits guilt?
parts.note: Plato's account of Socrates' speech at his trial bears this title, though in everyday speech the word means saying sorry

explanation.surface: A philosopher's courtroom defence that seems to concede guilt.
explanation.walkthrough: Plato's dialogue of Socrates' trial speech has this title in its old sense of formal defence; today it means owning up.
explanation.definitionFit: In the old sense a reasoned defence of a position; now an expression of regret for a wrong.

clue.text: Restraints preventing exaggeration of size of catch?

definitions.meaning: metal rings locked on a prisoner's wrists

definitions.text: preventing exaggeration of size of catch?
definitions.meaning: an angler shows how big a fish was by holding the arms wide apart, which tied wrists would stop

explanation.surface: Something to stop an angler boasting about the fish that got away.
explanation.definitionFit: Police manacles, which would also stop a fisherman stretching his arms to show a whopper.

clue.text: Anger Martin, falsely making public accusation

indicators.note: falsely means wrongly put, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Martin is angered by being falsely accused in public.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal charge read out in court against a defendant.

clue.text: Doss down with a half cured fish

indicators.note: a half means only the first three of the six letters are kept

explanation.surface: Sleeping rough with half a smoked herring.
explanation.walkthrough: A kipper is a cured herring; to doss down is British slang for sleeping in a makeshift bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for sleeping or a nap, as in roughing it for the night.

clue.text: Married man originally so addressed a lady

parts.note: Adam was the first man, the original of mankind

explanation.surface: A newly-wed husband greets a woman formally.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer read as a whole is also the famous palindrome Adam is said to have spoken to Eve.
explanation.definitionFit: A polite form of address for a woman, as in a shop assistant's greeting.

clue.text: This man advertised 76 trombones

parts.note: the conman hero of Meredith Willson's ..., who sings of seventy-six trombones, is called after this word

explanation.surface: A salesman promotes a huge brass band.
explanation.walkthrough: The Music Man is a Broadway musical whose hero sells band instruments; its best-known song is 'Seventy-Six Trombones'.
explanation.definitionFit: The word completing the title The ___ Man, the musical whose hero sells a town on a marching band.

clue.text: Doctor taking wine about to become violent

parts.note: Asti is an Italian sparkling wine
C, short for circa, means about

explanation.surface: A drinking doctor turns aggressive.
explanation.definitionFit: Extreme and forceful, as with harsh measures taken suddenly.

clue.text: High office to which one was summoned by bells

definitions.text: High office to which one was summoned by bells

parts.words: High office to which one was summoned by bells
parts.note: Dick Whittington heard Bow Bells call him back to become Lord Mayor of London

explanation.surface: Someone called by church bells to an important post.
explanation.walkthrough: In English legend Dick Whittington turned back on hearing Bow Bells chime 'Turn again, Whittington, thrice Lord Mayor of London'.
explanation.definitionFit: The office or term of a civic leader, which Whittington held three times.

clue.text: Being short of one key, this singer?

definitions.text: Being short of one key, this singer?

parts.words: Being short of one key, this singer?
parts.note: a soft, low-voiced singer of ballads who keeps to a narrow range, never straying far from one key

explanation.surface: A vocalist who cannot manage more than one key.
explanation.definitionFit: A singer of sentimental songs in a soft murmuring style, like Bing Crosby.

clue.text: Fishing right is about to be retained by Paul

indicators.note: being retained by something means being held inside it

parts.note: Paul Pry is the nosy hero of an old English comedy, so Paul suggests his surname
taken as written
CA, short for circa, means about

explanation.surface: Paul holds the angling rights to a stretch of river.
explanation.walkthrough: Paul Pry, from John Poole's 1825 play, became a byword for a busybody; CA is circa.
explanation.definitionFit: A legal term for the right to fish in another's waters.

clue.text: One final letter returned by this school's founder

definitions.text: One final letter returned by this school's founder

parts.words: One final letter returned by this school's founder
parts.note: the word one plus the alphabet's last letter Z, read backwards, spells Zeno, who founded a school of Greek philosophy

explanation.surface: A school's founder sends back one last letter.
explanation.walkthrough: Zeno of Citium taught in the Painted Porch (stoa) in Athens, giving his school its name.
explanation.definitionFit: A follower of the school of philosophy founded by Zeno, teaching calm indifference to pain and pleasure.

clue.text: It shows rejected acid entering into river

indicators.note: entering a word means going inside it

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: rejected suggests something thrown back, so the word acid is read backwards

explanation.surface: A chemist's report on acid that was refused and poured into a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It shows' is a cryptic definition of a pointer or gauge; 'rejected' signals the turnaround and 'entering' the container.
explanation.definitionFit: A dial, needle or pointer is a device whose job is to display a reading or state.

clue.text: Tie-in with curry here for a postprandial session

parts.note: a drawn game is a tie
taken as written
to curry a horse is to groom it with a comb

explanation.surface: Combining a tie with a hot curry for an after-dinner gathering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'curry' looks like the dish but is the verb for grooming a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: The room guests withdraw to after dinner, a parlour or lounge.

clue.text: Unprofessional number of minstrels

definitions.meaning: not of the clergy or a profession, amateur
a number is a song, and minstrels sang ballads

explanation.surface: Amateur musicians perform a song.
explanation.definitionFit: Lay people are non-specialists, and a lay is a narrative poem or song as sung by medieval minstrels.

clue.text: Dark outcome of burning the midnight oil

definitions.text: Dark outcome of burning the midnight oil

parts.words: Dark outcome of burning the midnight oil
parts.note: not late study but literal soot left by an oil light burning all night

explanation.surface: The gloomy result of studying late into the night.
explanation.definitionFit: A black pigment made from soot of burning oil, as from a lantern.

clue.text: Like Orsino's fancy or Respighi's boutique?

definitions.text: Like Orsino's fancy or Respighi's boutique?

parts.words: Like Orsino's fancy or Respighi's boutique?
parts.note: Orsino in Twelfth Night says fancy alone is high-flown in this way, and Respighi's ballet is La Boutique fantasque

explanation.surface: A comparison between a Shakespearean duke's imagination and a composer's shop.
explanation.walkthrough: Orsino's opening speech in Twelfth Night ends 'That it alone is high fantastical'; Respighi arranged Rossini's music for the ballet La Boutique fantasque.
explanation.definitionFit: Wildly imaginative or bizarre, the quality both literary references share.

clue.text: Man of the world by nature ill-disposed

indicators.note: disposed means set out or arranged, so the letters of the words before it are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A worldly person who is naturally unfriendly.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphen in 'ill-disposed' hides that 'ill' belongs to the fodder and only 'disposed' is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An inhabitant of the earth, from Latin tellus.

clue.text: Such words from the bench relevant about soldiers

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one word goes round another

parts.note: material evidence is relevant evidence
GIs are American soldiers

explanation.surface: A judge's remarks are pertinent to the troops on trial.
explanation.definitionFit: A judge or magistrate on the bench speaks in an authoritative, judicial manner.

clue.text: Number about.500 in a record set up by canal-boat

indicators.note: in places one group of letters inside another
in a down clue set up means written upwards, so the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: a log is a written record

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500

explanation.surface: A record of a large number set by a canal barge.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'set up' signals reading upwards; 'about' and 'in' are the two containers, the smaller one sitting inside the turned record.
explanation.definitionFit: The long black boat steered by a single oar on Venice's canals.

clue.text: Tree bark

definitions.meaning: the laurel, whose leaves flavour cooking
to howl as a hound does

explanation.surface: The covering of a tree trunk.
explanation.definitionFit: The laurel is so named as a tree, and hounds are said to howl this way when they corner prey.

clue.text: For a sword-bearer not hard to finish a bare-headed king

parts.note: bald means without hair on the head

indicators.note: not shows that the following word is taken away
to finish says the removal is from the end

parts.note: Richard is the name of several English kings
taken as the word itself

explanation.surface: A bald king finds it easy to finish holding a sword.
explanation.definitionFit: A belt worn over the shoulder that carries a sword.

clue.text: Guest band arranged for house in Bona

indicators.note: arranged means put in a new order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A visiting group of musicians plays for a household in Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: Bonn was the capital of West Germany, where its parliament sat.
explanation.definitionFit: The lower chamber of the German federal parliament, which sat in Bonn before reunification.

clue.text: Where the lovely girl is seen

indicators.note: is seen means the letters can be spotted within the clue words

explanation.surface: Where a pretty young woman might be found.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's name, popular in Edwardian times.

clue.text: By no means bright putting money in one

indicators.note: in places one word inside another

parts.note: a unit is one
L stands for pounds (libra), British money

explanation.surface: Investing cash in a single scheme is hardly clever.
explanation.definitionFit: Dark, without lamps lit, so not bright in the sense of light.

clue.text: Sort of saw 6 dn. for the Muses coming up

indicators.note: in a down clue coming up means written upwards, so the letters are reversed

parts.note: 6 down is music, and the Muses were nine, so music for nine is a nonet

explanation.surface: A tool for the nine Muses to play with.
explanation.definitionFit: A fine-toothed carpenter's saw used for cutting joints.

clue.text: One more alias for unnamed member of team?

definitions.text: alias for unnamed member of team?
definitions.meaning: ... is the stand-in name printed on British team sheets for a player not yet chosen

explanation.surface: An unnamed extra player is listed under a false name.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a team list may show 'A. N. Other' for a player still to be named.
explanation.definitionFit: It means an additional one, and split as initials it gives the placeholder name for an unknown team member.

clue.text: Perch caught with it?

definitions.meaning: an old measure of length, five and a half yards
a fishing pole used to land the fish

explanation.surface: A freshwater fish hooked by an angler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perch' looks like the fish, but here it is the old unit of length, also called a pole.
explanation.definitionFit: A rod, pole or perch is the same old length, and a fish is caught with a fishing rod.

clue.text: Barchester Pie so called in a letter from Greece

definitions.meaning: the pen name under which the novel Barchester Pie appeared
a character of the Greek alphabet, short o

explanation.surface: A pie from the cathedral town gets a Greek name in a letter.
explanation.walkthrough: Barchester is Trollope's fictional cathedral town; the later novel Barchester Pie carried a Greek letter as its author's pen name.
explanation.definitionFit: The fifteenth letter of the Greek alphabet, little o, also used as a pseudonym.

clue.text: Early riser does a turn round a S African village

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so one piece goes about another
doing a turn suggests turning about, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a lark is a person who gets up early

explanation.surface: Someone up at dawn walks around an African settlement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'does a turn' turns LARK into KRAL, which goes round A.
explanation.definitionFit: A traditional enclosed settlement of huts in southern Africa.

clue.text: Monk is a Benedictine at home I am able to conclude

parts.note: Dom is the title given to a Benedictine monk
in means at home
taken as written
can means am able

explanation.surface: A monk declares himself Benedictine and able to finish.
explanation.definitionFit: A friar of the order founded by St Dominic, a Black Friar.
